undirected_baseline_unchanged.rationale: CO-006c extended CO-006 / CO-006b in place by adding a directed branch — undirected cells continue to track the figures captured in .codefuse/tracking/perf/ALGO-CO-006.json and ALGO-CO-006b.json (variance within ±15% on short -m 3s runs).

python_igraph.notes: python-igraph supports directed edge-betweenness community via the same C entrypoint with a `directed=True` flag. The directed-path-10 case is dominated by per-call overhead (~10-20 µs) in both runtimes.

notes: Directed Brandes forward pass walks the OUT-incidence list (graph.incident with mode OUT) instead of the undirected ALL list, so the per-vertex traversal cost is halved on average. The directed dendrogram pulls m iterations of Brandes-OUT — the directed-two-triangles-bridge cell (6v 7e) completes in 8.3 µs unweighted vs the undirected two-K4-bridge (8v 13e) at ~17 µs.

C reference rule preserved: `if (!directed) eb /= 2.0;`. Directed `eb` is left un-halved, which is what the C, Python, and R reference layers test. Documented as an integration test (`directed_betweenness_is_not_halved`).

Per-level Q dispatch: directed graphs use `modularity_directed` (unweighted) or `modularity_weighted_directed` (weighted; introduced in this AWU); undirected continue to use the matching undirected modularity. The closure `level_q` collapses the four-way switch into one branch site to keep the dendrogram-replay loop readable.

Modularity_weighted_directed mirrors modularity_directed: per-cluster contribution e_kk - r * (a_k * b_k / m), with a_k = sum of weighted out-strengths and b_k = sum of weighted in-strengths inside the cluster, normalised by the total weighted edge sum m. Falls through to modularity_weighted when the graph is undirected so callers get a single entry point.

Directed Brandes uses lowest-eid tie-break on three-way ties — captured by the smoke test `directed_two_triangles_bridge_runs_cleanly` so any future re-ordering shows up as a deterministic-but-different removal order, not a silent regression.
